analysis.evidence: Shelah is the subject of חַי ‘he lived’ and וַיּוֹלֶד ‘he fathered’. The latter takes אֶת עֵבֶר ‘Eber’ as its direct object, identifying Shelah as Eber’s father.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ prefixes the masculine personal name שֶׁלַח.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה gives the duration of חַי. Shelah lived thirty years before he fathered Eber.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with שֶׁלַח (Shelah) as its subject.
analysis.sense: live, be alive; live so many years
